accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE National Curriculum (2013) English Years 5-6 reading comprehension statements 'recommending books that they have read to their peers, giving reasons for their choices', 'identifying and discussing themes and conventions in and across a wide range of writing' and 'making comparisons within and across books'. Genre (mystery, adventure, fantasy) and theme (friendship, standing up to a bully) are used as KS2 glossary-style terms, with m4 and the challenge separating genre, theme and physical features. Books and readers are invented, as the adult text says, so no plot facts can be wrong.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips teachers report in book-talk and in CLPE's Reading for Pleasure guidance: recommending your own favourite (prediction option 'Your own favourite book', challenge 'Your favourite war story', m6), praise without reasons ('It's the best book ever', 'awesome', 'It's amazing'), surface links by length, cover or date (link step and challenge), and retelling the ending (spoiler step, m2).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrecbk is a recommendation workshop: reader cards with tastes matched to book cards, reason chips dragged into Specific or Too vague bins, Sam's five-line recommendation where spoilers are tapped and turn red, 'If you liked A, try B because...' links, and a four-slot recommendation builder with a Check that names the weak slot. flagopine, flagbook and flagauth teach opinions, book features and author purpose with different mechanics, and the 30% shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step produces one part of the final recommendation: step 1 shows that the right book depends on the reader, step 2 that a reason must name a feature, step 3 what counts as a spoiler, step 4 that comparisons work through genre or theme. Step 5 then makes the learner assemble all four parts and only passes when each one is strong, so the rule is discovered before the text confirms it.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'What matters most when you pick a book for a friend?' (Your own favourite book), 'Which reason helps a friend most?' (It is the best book ever) and 'Should you tell your friend how the book ends?' (Yes, so they know it is good). Each is tested straight away by the matching, sorting and spoiler tasks, and the kit confirms or corrects the pick.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with shuffled buttons and ten m= messages tied to the specific wrong choice, e.g. 'Length, page count or chapter count do not tell a reader if they will enjoy the story', 'Hardback is how the book is made. A theme is a big idea the story explores' and 'What someone else thought is not about the book'. Lab mistakes also get specific messages, such as why Storm Island does not suit Leo.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK grade 3.7 (learner limit 6.5) with short sentences and worked examples of good and weak lines. Adult text scores 9.4 (limit 9.5), quotes the curriculum statements and names the KS2 terms genre, theme, narrator and plot structure. Canvas cards use 14 px text on a phone and wrap inside their boxes.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph gives one rule with an example (start with the reader; give a specific reason; compare by genre or theme; keep the surprises). The family tip is a concrete turn-taking game with three rules, and the content gate's filler patterns all passed.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots of every step after Show me, in light and dark, show one card per row with wrapped 14 px text, bins wide enough to drop on, and spoiler cards turning red. The first pass had 12.5 px card text, which was too small, so the font and phone canvas height (tall 1.55) were raised. Every canvas action also has a button (Give Maya..., Specific/Too vague, Spoiler?, Change: part, Check).

accessibility.evidence: The pipeline walk ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors. The canvas aria-label repeats the current prompt or feedback (e.g. 'Maya: Loved a detective story. Likes to solve puzzles. Tap the book that fits her.'), feedback goes to the aria-live line, and drag-only actions have labelled button alternatives.
